steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and mushrooms; season with salt and black pepper. Cook and stir until mushrooms are dark and juicy, about 5 minutes. Off heat, stir in bread crumbs. Set aside.

Place chicken breasts, one at a time, between 2 sheets of heavy plastic (resealable freezer bags work well) on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound breasts with the smooth side of a meat mallet to a 1/4-inch thickness.

Lay 1 breast onto a work surface; place 1 slice ham on top. Spoon about 3 tablespoons mushroom mixture onto ham; top with about 2 1/2 tablespoons Havarti cheese. Roll breast to enclose filling. Firmly wrap roll with 2 strips bacon; secure with toothpicks. Place roll in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Repeat with remaining breasts, ham, mushroom mixture, Havarti cheese, and bacon.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink and fillings melted and hot, about 35 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers of rolls should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Remove rolls from the oven. Carefully set an oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Turn on the broiler and return rolls to the oven. Broil until bacon is brown, 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom Melt Stuffed Chicken
raw_recipe.description: In this mushroom melt stuffed chicken recipe, chicken breasts are rolled around a mushroom filling, ham, and Havarti-pepper cheese, and wrapped in bacon.
raw_recipe.name: Mushroom Melt Stuffed Chicken

review.reviewBody: YUMMMM!!!!! I have to say that we totally LOVED this chicken! I made a couple of changes tho :-) I always do... I scaled this recipe down to 6..well I used 3 whole chx breast and cut em in half then pounded them out and had 6 pcs. I used EVOO and 2T butter to saute my cremini mushrooms, onion and garlic in. After the mush turned soft, I added a lil (only a sm amt, bc the bacon will have alot of salt) S&P. I added about 2T heavy cream to the mush mix then about 2T (ish) It. brd. crumbs. I didn't shred anything...I used 1 lg garlic clove as well. I used sliced Havarti cheese. (slice BF ham, hav ch, mush mix, then put it on top of my thin chx brst and roll it.) I also used balsamic vinegar to brush on my chicken after I rolled them...it added another depth of flavor. Absolutley use the bacon pcs on the chicken, bc OMG they are PHEONOMINAL!! Be sure to broil for 10 mins after cooking!!! I put my chx on a rack on a foil covered baking sheet...less mess. We LOVEDDDDD these...I made Easy Mushroom Rice from this site...if you want that to be awesome, also check out my review :-) Thanks sooooooooo much for sharing your awesome recipe, dude, you rock!

I cut the recipe to 1 chicken breast, which makes 2 servings. I actually made the mushroom recipe the way I make mushroom empanadas (minced, sauteed with dill, scallions, parsley, cheddar, breadcrumbs and a little heavy cream), but then followed the rest of the recipe. I used honey ham over the mushroom recipe and used 2 slices of bacon per serving. you really want to cover the chicken with the bacon so it doesnt dry out on the ends. my boyfriend's only suggestion was to add some type of sweet glaze on top. There was a user who used balsmic on top, and i just forgot to do it, but next time i will brush the bacon with it prior to putting under broiler. Also, i would broil for 5 minutes, not 10. i did it for 6 minutes and the ends seems a little dry. that is why i mention the bacon covering. My boyfriend said it was good and he definitely wants me to make it again. You could really stuff it with anything you want. the breadcrumbs are necessary so that the filling doesnt turn juicy and run out completely. i used about 1/8-1/4 c of fresh breadcrumbs .

I made this for my husband and I . Only needed 2 chicken breasts . Made the stuffing per recipe. Had some leftover which I added garlic ,broccoli , snow peas ,red and orange peppers plus my frozen corn kernels. This was continued for a stir fry accompaniment..... Also had no bacon so used prosciutto for wrap.. cooked on bbq in foil When correct internal temp was reached . I unwrapped foil and gave it a couple of mins more. I was a little unadventurous with the spud choice and chose baked. My husband was very delighted and said it was delicious. My Mission accomplished .

This took a little extra effort than most baked chicken dishes, but with some tweaking to suit my tastes, it was fun preparing it, and we enjoyed eating it. It was nice to have something a little more “fussy” and interesting. When I chopped up the mushrooms and onions, I did so till the mixture was a fine mince and added some garlic as well. (I meant to deglaze the pan with a little white wine, which would have been nice, but I forgot) I skipped the bread crumbs entirely and just as I suspected, we didn’t miss them. As for the cheese, wouldn’t you know I had just about everything BUT Havarti in the fridge but there are any number of acceptable substitutes – in a pinch any semi-soft cheese will do. I used a Pepper Jack for mine, but in consideration of Hubs’ sensitive innards I used just a mild Cheddar in his. Rather than piling the mushroom-onion mixture and the cheese on the chicken in a blob, I spread everything over the surface of each breast and then rolled it up pinwheel-style. Wrapping each with two slices of bacon was not only too much, it resulted in the bacon underneath staying unattractively fatty and gloppy. One slice, cut in two pieces and laid over the top, would have worked much better. Not only did we not miss the bread crumbs, I don’t think I’d miss the cheese either. You wouldn’t be sacrificing any flavor or compromising the dish by eliminating both.

This had a great flavor. I made it as written except I couldn't find the cheese listed so I just used regular sliced Havarti. I did slightly precook the bacon before I wrapped it around the chicken breasts and when it was finished baking, the bacon was nicely browned and I didn't have to worry about the underside of it being partly raw. Because of precooking, it didn't need to go under the broiler. Our chicken was moist and we thought all the flavors went together nicely. I would make this again.

This is SO good! I made a couple very small changes but nothing that would change the overall concept of the recipe. The first change is I made this with chicken thighs instead of breasts as we don’t like chicken breasts because they are very dry and chewy. Because I used thigh meat I made this as a casserole instead of a stuffed dish. The thighs were put into a dish, the Black Forest ham went next, the mushroom stuffing was put on top (I did sauté some garlic with the mushroom and onion and used panko crumbs as that’s all I had),then the havarti cheese and last the bacon (turkey bacon for us). Cooked it for about a half hour. So delicious! Because it was more of a casserole I didn’t have to deal with the hassle of flattening and rolling and pinning with toothpicks.

Incredibly tasty! I bought 6 chicken cutlets already pounded out. Used the called for amount of onion and mushrooms, added garlic and then only used about 1/3 C of italian seasoned bread crumbs. I used sliced havarti because my grocery store didn't have shredded. Didn't use toothpicks because I used the bacon to tie in the chicken and mushroom stuffing. Sprinkled balsamic vinegar on the top of the bacon per another reviewer's suggestion. Low broiled for the last 6-7 min and then put the remaining 3-4 min on 425 while I was finishing the sides. I was so happy with this recipe and I can't wait to make it again!

This is delicious! I made this last night for seven guests, and they raved asking for the recipe. A few minor changes: added a minimum of salt to the stuffing as well as a heart healthy lower sodium Black Forest ham, a package of rehydrated mixed mushrooms as well as button mushrooms, unseasoned breadcrumbs and chopped fresh basil and oregano in the mix. Could not find Havarti Pepper cheese but used Havarti Jalapeño, It took an hour to bake before putting under the broiler for ten minutes. Moist and so tasty. Will make again!

This is super delicious! I did make a few minor changes (I usually do). I used swiss cheese because that is what I had in the fridge. As the chicken cooked, I was afraid it was going to be dry. So...I broiled the bacon on top of the chicken in the dish it was cooking in. Then I took some Cream of Mushroom soup, reduced it w/ some white wine, then put it back in oven until the sauce was bubbly. Soooo yummy!

Whoa—don’t need any side salad with this—a complete and delicious meal all by itself. I added arugula into the filling and some baby spinach. Just 1 piece of thick cut pepper bacon on each breast. Excellent!! Pinned each rolled breadt with a metal turkey pin.. Don’t think toothpicks will do it. Watch your broiler at the end—bacon will brown quick. Super delicious!!

Awesome recipe. I made it more "paleo" by substituting parm crisps for the bread crumbs and using boneless chicken thighs instead of breasts. I also finished it up on my grill instead of under the broiler. Not only will I make it again, it is going into my regular "rotation."

This was excellent! I even made it without the bacon (don't judge me :). I rubbed the top of the breasts with a little oil and spread bread crumbs over the top to keep the surface from drying out. My wife loved it. It's a definite repeat!

Made it for my Birthday dinner and used pepper jack cheese instead of Havarti 
it had a little bite but over all it was very good

I kinda cheated this recipe, instead of flatting the chicken breast, I cut it open and stuffed it with all the ingredients. I also used can mushrooms, All in all this was a GREAT recipe. It cut down the prep time. This is a great meal with potatoes and green vegetables.
as of right I used garlic powder onion powder season salt and sage. stay tuned for results. it was amazing nice and juicy amazing flavor
Amazing! I modified a little and finely diced onion and added green bell pepper with the mushroom mixture and used Italian bread crumbs and perfect!!
This is so yummy!
So easy to make . I used thin sliced Harvarti cheese. Any number of cheeses would work with this recipe. My family loved it.

I liked this but hubby thought it was just ok - which was a little disappointing because chicken, bacon and mushrooms?? Should have been an automatic win. I think it was a bit soggy, couldn’t get the bacon to quite crisp up, and I turned the chicken about half way through to try to avoid soggy bacon on the bottom. Didn’t quite work. May try it again.
Loved it , use thin bacon
